item.title: ECB Rate Decision: Lagarde Set to Keep Policy Unchanged to Gauge Iran War Risks
item.description: The European Central Bank will probably keep interest rates on hold on Thursday, buying time to assess the fallout of renewed fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: Half of Economists Still See BOJ Waiting Until December to Hike
item.description: Half of surveyed economists still expect the Bank of Japan to wait until December to bump its benchmark interest rate higher, with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government seen as a key obstacle to further action, according to a Bloomberg survey.

item.title: China’s Semight Is Said to Mull Hong Kong Listing After 2,200% Stock Rise
item.description: Semight Instruments Co. is considering a second listing in Hong Kong, people familiar with the matter said, after shares of the Chinese maker of test instruments for semiconductors surged roughly 2,200% since their debut in April.

item.title: Indonesian Stocks Rise 20% From Low in June, Set for Bull Market
item.description: A rally in Indonesian stocks put the nation’s benchmark index on track for a bull market, helped by a regional rebound as well as a recent credit-rating announcement.

item.title: India Rate-Hike Odds Rise as Pricey Crude Stokes Inflation Risk
item.description: The swap market is pricing in at least a 25-basis-point hike at the October meeting.

item.title: China Solar Lobby Says Fewer Installs Mark Sustainable Shift
item.description: China’s solar lobby said the industry is on a more sustainable track, after a policy shift drove a 66% decline in installations in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Asian Chip Stocks Climb as Alphabet Spending Revives AI Momentum
item.description: Asian semiconductor stocks rose as Alphabet Inc.’s plans to spend up to $200 billion this year on artificial intelligence computing power refueled optimism over trickle-down benefits.

item.title: Fund Managers Want Taiwan Regulators to Lift a Mobile Phone Ban
item.description: When fund managers in Taiwan arrive at work each morning, they have to lock away their mobile phones before the stock and bond markets open, and can’t retrieve their devices until the end of the trading day.

item.title: TSMC-Supplier LCY Says KKR Will Exit, Allowing Faster US Growth
item.description: Private equity giant KKR & Co. plans to gradually sell its stake in LCY Group’s business, the Taiwan chemical maker’s chairman said, paving the way for the family-controlled company to accelerate the expansion of its semiconductor material operations.

item.title: India Silver Imports Slump as New Licensing Disrupts Shipments
item.description: Silver imports into India have slowed sharply as a new licensing regime disrupted shipments, pushing local premiums to a multi-month high.

item.title: Australian Employment Soars in June, Bolstering Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Australian employment surged in June, extending the previous month’s gains, underscoring the ongoing strength in the nation’s labor market and stoking bets on another interest-rate increase.

item.title: Aditya Birla Fund Manager Bets on Earnings Growth to Lift Stocks
item.description: Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Co., one of India’s largest money managers, is betting on a recovery in corporate earnings to drive gains in the nation’s equity market.

item.title: Khosla Ventures in Talks to Raise $5.5 Billion in New Funds
item.description: Early OpenAI backer Khosla Ventures is discussing raising as much as $5.5 billion for its latest set of venture investment funds, a haul that would amount to its largest fundraising event in its two-decade history, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Mexican Mayor Shot Dead in his Office After Surviving Earlier Hit
item.description: Armed assailants gunned down the mayor of a small Mexican city just south of the country’s capital in his office in the latest case of suspected gangland violence targeting a local official.

item.title: Yen’s Slump in Trade-Weighted Gauge Shows Its Broad-Based Drop
item.description: While the yen’s plunge to a four-decade low against the dollar has dominated headlines, a broader gauge of the currency’s strength is sending an equally worrying signal for Japan.

item.title: Ebola Deaths Top 1,000 in Congo as Response Trails Fastest-Spreading Outbreak
item.description: Confirmed Ebola deaths in Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed 1,000, prompting Africa’s top public health official to warn the outbreak could become one of the worst on record unless transmission is rapidly brought under control.

item.title: OpenAI Models Spent Hours on Hack That Usually Takes Weeks
item.description: When OpenAI’s advanced artificial intelligence models breached AI startup Hugging Face’s internal systems last week, they spent mere hours carrying out a hack that would have taken a skilled human far longer, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: China’s Psibot Becomes Latest AI Startup to Hit $1 Billion Value
item.description: PsiBot is raising close to $100 million of funding at a $1.48 billion valuation, joining a growing roster of Chinese AI startups capitalizing on interest in the burgeoning field.

item.title: China’s High-Profile Funds Ditch Consumer Stocks to Chase AI
item.description: Some high-profile Chinese funds heavily invested in consumer names are pivoting to AI stocks, a bet that may boost returns but also leaves them more vulnerable to the sector’s volatility.

item.title: Nasdaq to Kick Off Tiny Companies Faster After SEC Approves Rule
item.description: Nasdaq Inc. will change its rules to make it easier to kick off flailing businesses as regulators zero in on wild market swings and allegations of manipulation that have plagued trading in so-called microcap stocks.

item.title: Uber Cuts 10% of Customer Service Jobs, Citing ‘Embrace’ of AI
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. said it has cut 10% of jobs within its customer service operations as part of a broader effort to simplify its ranks and “embrace artificial intelligence.”

item.title: Gold Holds Gain as Dip-Buying Counters Inflation Fears From War
item.description: Gold held gains on dip-buying even as hostilities in the Middle East pushed oil prices to multiweek highs, rekindling concerns that US inflationary pressure could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

item.title: Hong Kong’s Offshore Yuan Market Evolves Into Global Funding Hub
item.description: A record pile of yuan in Hong Kong is making its way to corporate loans while driving a surge in capital market activity, signaling that China’s drive to internationalize its currency is advancing.

item.title: South Korea’s Economy Beats Estimates as Chip Boom Continues
item.description: South Korea’s economy grew faster than expected in the second quarter, driven by an artificial intelligence-fueled chip boom that supports the case for further interest-rate increases.

item.title: South Africa Set for Rate Hike as Inflation Flares: Day Guide
item.description: South Africa’s central bank appears set to raise borrowing costs for a second consecutive meeting, as fresh price pressures emerge from intensified fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: Coinbase to Expand Singapore Team Amid Global Restructuring: BT
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global Inc. is looking to expand its headcount in Singapore to 200 by the end of the year, up from 150, the Business Times reported Wednesday.

item.title: Musk Says Micron Gave Tesla ‘Significant’ Supply of Memory Chips
item.description: Micron Technology Inc. recently gave Tesla Inc. a “significant allocation” of memory chips, according to Elon Musk, helping meet the automaker’s demand for an increasingly precious commodity.

item.title: Amazon Investigated Over Chinese Influence by US Senate Panel
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. is being investigated by the Senate Small Business Committee for allegedly letting China influence the company’s online marketplace, according to a document reviewed by Bloomberg and two people interviewed as part of the investigation.

item.title: US Stock Futures Slip on Alphabet, Oil Advances: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equity-index futures declined after Alphabet Inc.’s spending plans intensified concerns about the payoff from the industry’s aggressive artificial intelligence buildout. Oil extended its rally.

item.title: Wall Street Banks Trading Parts of $35 Billion AI Chip Deal
item.description: Wall Street banks have started buying and selling an initial piece of a $35 billion financing package for Broadcom Inc. and Anthropic PBC’s AI infrastructure expansion, with the biggest private credit deal ever now being offered to a wider pool of investors.
